newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria frees FIS leader Abassi Madani from jail.
newsitem.headline: Algeria frees FIS leader Abassi Madani from jail.

text.p: Algeria on Tuesday freed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) chief Abassi Madani, a military prosecutor's office said in a statement.
The statement, carried by the official Algerian news agency APS, said the measure was a "release on parole".

Madani, who is FIS president, was arrested along with his hardline deputy Ali Belhadj in June 1991 and sentenced the next year to 12 years' jail by a military court for threatening Algeria's security.
His "release on parole" came as clear appeasement signal by President Liamine Zeroual's government towards moderate Islamists in the violence-ridden country.

It also came a week after a FIS provisional leader Abdelkader Hachani walked out of an Algiers prison just hours after being sentenced to five years in jail. He had served that time in detention but the prosecutor had asked for 10 years imprisonment.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS had taken a huge lead.
